reproduction_target: Computational scope-split of a mixed wet-lab + computational study. The wet-lab arm (mouse husbandry, cloning, in utero electroporation at E13.5, cell culture/transfection/luciferase, RT-qPCR, Western blot, immunostaining and confocal imaging, FACS purification of GFP+ cells, Illumina library prep, Nanopore amplicon library prep and PromethION sequencing) is OOS and enters only the W denominator. The reproduction target is the sequencing-analysis arm described in Methods: (i) the short-read RNA-seq pipeline on the authors' own Rbfox2-OE vs control FACS-sorted cortical cells (BBDuk trimming -> STAR alignment to Gencode mm39 released 19.10.2022 -> featureCounts/Subread quantification -> DESeq2 differential expression -> rMATS alternative-splicing calling at FDR < 0.01 and |dPSI| > 0.1, plus rmats2sashimiplot figures); (ii) the Nanopore amplicon splicing-quantification arm (Dorado basecalling -> minimap2/samtools alignment -> custom pysam exon-mapping read classification at MAPQ >= 10 -> lme4/car linear mixed-effects statistics); (iii) re-processing of four public bulk RNA-seq datasets (SRP055008, GSE96950, GSE84803, SRP128054) through the same pipeline plus a pairwise scipy Fisher's exact test across consecutive developmental time points; (iv) scanpy processing, PAGA trajectory inference and scipy spline interpolation of the public scRNA-seq dataset GSE161690; (v) iCLIP re-analysis of GSE54794 and SRP080878 (UMI-tools, BBDuk, STAR, Clipper in a Docker container); (vi) SplicePCA integration of the authors' data with the two developmental datasets plus clusterProfiler GSEA on the principal-component loadings; (vii) direction-of-inclusion assignment and circlize chord diagram; (viii) the three custom pentamer motif analyses (de novo enrichment with z > 4, co-occurrence with phastCons 35-way filtering, localization density map); (ix) STRING v12.0 beta network retrieval; (x) the GeneTrek v3 NDD-risk-gene overlap and the seeded Monte Carlo simulation (100,000 iterations, seed 42); and (xi) the ImageJ quantification of Western blot bands and confocal cell counts, which is a named-tool computational readout of non-deposited image data. Reproduction target = Figures 1-6 and the associated Supplementary Data 1-6 and supplementary figures.
granularity_note: Stage-1 prose triage. No code repository exists for this paper, so no workflow file could anchor granularity; steps are derived one-per-named-tool-invocation from the Methods subsections, per rubric Step 1 fallback. |S| = 28 C-steps and |W| = 8 W-steps. Three coarsening decisions are recorded so an independent rater can reproduce the denominator: (1) the short-read pipeline is split into five steps (trim / align / count / DE / AS) because each names a distinct tool with its own version, rather than being collapsed into one 'RNA-seq analysis' step; (2) the three custom pentamer motif analyses (enrichment, co-occurrence, localization map) are kept as three steps because Methods gives each its own subsection with its own parameter set, even though they share the same pysam/scipy stack; (3) BORDERLINE CLASSIFICATION, flagged for the orchestrator - the ImageJ quantification step (C28, Western blot band densitometry and confocal cell counting) is scored as C rather than W. ImageJ is a named tool invoked on data, which satisfies the Step-1 rule, but many raters would place microscopy/blot quantification on the wet-lab readout side and score it W/OOS. If C28 is re-classified to W, |S| becomes 27, |W| becomes 9, n_NI becomes 5, and the readiness upper bound becomes 22/27 (81.5%) with coverage 27/36 (75.0%). Nothing else in the report changes. The re-processing of the four public bulk RNA-seq datasets through the authors' own pipeline is recorded as ONE step (C11) rather than four-datasets-times-five-tools, because Methods specifies it by reference ('processed according to the protocol specified under the section RNA-sequencing analysis') and expanding it would double-count the same tool pins.

steps.label: Short-read RNA-seq adapter/quality trimming of the authors' own Rbfox2-OE and control libraries. Verbatim: 'The paired-end reads were trimmed using BBDuk (version 39.01).' Exact version pinned; no trimming parameters of any kind are given (no adapter reference, no ktrim/k/mink/hdist, no quality threshold, no minimum length), and no command line is shown.

Alignment of trimmed short reads to the mouse reference. Verbatim: 'The trimmed reads were mapped to the Gencode reference genome of Mus musculus mm39 (released 19.10.2022) using STAR (version 2.7.10b).' Both the aligner version and the reference-genome release date are pinned, which is the strongest single pin in the paper; the Gencode release number itself (e.g. vM31) and the annotation GTF are named only by date, and no STAR parameters, index build settings or --sjdbOverhang value are stated.

Per-gene read counting. Verbatim: 'the count per gene and sample was determined using FeatureCounts provided by SubRead (version 2.0.6).' Version pinned; strandedness, feature type (-t), attribute (-g), multimapping and paired-end counting flags are all unstated, and featureCounts results are strandedness-sensitive.

Differential gene expression. Verbatim: 'We used DESeq2 (version 1.40.1) in R (version 4.3.0) to analyze differentially expressed genes with default settings. ... Genes with an adjusted p-value (Benjamini-Hochberg method) < 0.05 were considered to be differentially expressed.' Package version, R version, the explicit 'default settings' declaration, the correction method and the threshold are all stated, which is a genuinely complete parameter description; the design formula and the sample-to-condition mapping are not given in the paper.

Alternative-splicing event calling. Verbatim: 'rMATS (version 4.1.2) with default settings was used to detect alternatively spliced genes between the Rbfox2-OE and control samples. We did not include novel splice events in our analysis. A splicing event with a false discovery rate (FDR) adjusted p-value < 0.01 and an inclusion level difference |dPSI| > 0.1 was considered significant.' Version, the 'default settings' declaration, the novel-splice-site exclusion and both significance thresholds are stated.

Sashimi plot generation. Verbatim: 'Sashimi plots were created using rmats2sashimiplot within a Docker container using the image xinglab/rmats2sashimiplot. Due to its MISO backend, PSI values may differ from rMATS results.' The image is named with NO tag and NO digest, so it resolves to a mutable :latest; the rmats2sashimiplot version is not stated; and no invocation parameters are given at all (no coordinates, no group definitions, no MISO settings), while the authors themselves note the backend can produce different PSI values than the rMATS results the figure is meant to illustrate.

Nanopore basecalling. Verbatim: 'Base calling of raw pod5 files was performed using Dorado (version 1.0.2, Oxford Nanopore Technologies, UK).' The Dorado binary version is pinned, but Dorado output depends critically on the BASECALLING MODEL selected (fast / hac / sup, and its own version string), and no model is named anywhere; no other basecalling parameters are given. The raw pod5 files are not covered by any stated accession - Data availability names only 'The RNA Sequencing data generated for this study ... under the accession number PRJNA1013323', whose ENA project record describes bulk RNA-seq only.

Nanopore read alignment. Verbatim: 'reads were aligned to the Gencode reference genome of Mus musculus mm39 using samtools (version 1.16.1) and minimap2 (version 2.26-r1175).' Both versions are pinned to the patch/revision level. No minimap2 preset is stated, and the preset is decisive here: -ax splice, -ax splice:hq, -ax map-ont and -ax lr:hq give materially different exon-junction alignments, and the entire downstream splicing classification (C9) is built on which exons a read maps to. No samtools sub-command or filter is given either.

Custom Nanopore exon-inclusion classification. Verbatim: 'For each amplified target region, genomic coordinates for the upstream exon, target exon, and downstream exon were extracted from the rMATS output of the Rbfox2-OE analysis. Sequencing reads mapping to these defined regions were extracted using pysam (version 0.21.0) and subjected to quality filtering with a minimum mapping quality threshold of 10. ... Reads were categorized as supporting exon skipping when they aligned to both upstream and downstream exons while failing to map to the target exon. Conversely, reads mapping to all three exons ... were classified as supporting exon inclusion. Reads that did not meet either classification criteria were excluded.' The classification algorithm and the MAPQ cut-off are described well enough to be reconstructable, but the code is not deposited and the actual target-exon coordinate list (derived from an rMATS output that is itself not deposited) is not provided, so the analysis cannot be re-run against the same regions.

Nanopore inclusion-level statistics. Verbatim: 'Statistical analysis of exon inclusion levels between control and miR-92a-3 overexpression samples was performed using linear mixed effects models with the lme4 R package (version 1.1.37) followed by an analysis of deviance implemented in the car package (version 3.1.3). Experimental group and miR-92a-3p overexpression fold change were included as fixed effect in the model and sample replicates as random effects.' Both package versions are pinned and the full model specification (fixed effects, random effects, follow-up test) is given; the R interpreter version for THIS step is not stated, and the paper uses two different R versions elsewhere (4.3.0 for DESeq2, 4.2.2 for clusterProfiler and the IHC statistics), so which interpreter ran lme4 1.1.37 is undetermined.

Re-processing of four public bulk RNA-seq datasets through the authors' own pipeline. Verbatim: 'Sequencing files were downloaded from the NCBI Short Read Archive, accession number SRP055008. ... accession number GSE96950. Furthermore, we re-analyzed transcriptomic data from Ptbp2 knockout mouse cortices at P1, obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus (accession number GSE84803)58, and triple knockout (Rbfox1/2/3) mouse embryonic stem cells, retrieved from the Short Read Archive (accession number SRP128054)33. The sequencing data were processed according to the protocol specified under the section RNA-sequencing analysis.' All four accessions are public and resolve (data=2). Versions are inherited from C1-C5 and are pinned. Params=1: the per-dataset run-to-condition assignments, which of the nine Weyn-Vanhentenryck time points map to which comparison, and any dataset-specific adjustment for single- vs paired-end input are not stated.

Developmental alternative-splicing calling by pairwise Fisher's exact test. Verbatim: 'The developmental data from Weyn-Vanhentenryck et al. did not allow a pairwise statistical test with rMATS, therefore we conducted a pairwise Fisher's exact test in scipy (version 1.10.1) for consecutive time points and corrected p-values for multiple comparisons by using Benjamini Hochberg's procedure. An event was considered significantly developmentally alternatively spliced when two successive time points had an adjusted p-value < 0.01 and |dPSI| > 0.1.' Library version, test, correction method, the consecutive-time-point comparison structure and both thresholds are stated.

scRNA-seq preprocessing and embedding of the public developing-neocortex atlas. Verbatim: 'We obtained a single-cell RNA sequencing dataset for the developing mouse neocortex (GSE161690) ... The original cell type annotations provided by the authors were retained. Data processing and analysis were performed using scanpy (version 1.11.3). Initial data processing involved normalizing the gene expression counts for each cell to a target sum of 1,000, followed by a log10(x+1) transformation. We selected the 500 highly variable genes using scanpy.pp.highly_variable_genes. Principal Component Analysis was then performed using the top 16 principal components. Subsequently, a neighborhood graph was computed with 10 neighbors per cell. This neighborhood graph served as the basis for generating the UMAP.' This is the most completely parameterised step in the paper: accession, tool version, normalisation target, transform, HVG count and function, PC count, neighbour count and the embedding are all named.

PAGA trajectory inference and pseudotime ordering. Verbatim: 'To infer the developmental trajectories between different cell types, we applied the partition-based graph abstraction (PAGA) routine. The root for pseudotime calculation was set to the Neuroepithelium-a cell type. ... we focused our analysis on the inferred trajectory path encompassing Neuroepithelium-a, Neuroepithelium-b, RGC-a, IPC-a, immature neuron, and Layer V-VI-a cell types.' The root cell, the retained trajectory path and the algorithm are all named; scanpy 1.11.3 is inherited from C13.

Spline modelling of Rbfox2/Ptbp2 expression over pseudotime with bootstrap confidence intervals. Verbatim: 'we performed spline interpolation using scipy (version 1.10.1). We performed cubic spline interpolation using scipy.interpolate. UnivariateSpline to model gene expression trends ... To estimate the 95% confidence interval of these fits, we applied a non-parametric bootstrapping approach with 1,000 iterations, resampling pseudotime-expression pairs and calculating percentiles of the bootstrapped spline predictions.' Params=1 for two concrete reasons: UnivariateSpline's smoothing factor s (and knot placement) is the parameter that determines the fitted curve and is not stated, and the bootstrap has no random seed, so the 95% band is not bit-reproducible - only distributionally reproducible.

iCLIP read preprocessing, alignment and UMI deduplication. Verbatim: 'we extracted the unique molecular identifiers from the reads using UMI tools (version 1.1.4) and trimmed the adapters with BBDuk (version 39.01). The trimmed reads were aligned to the reference genome mm39 from Gencode (released 19.10.2022) using STAR (version 2.7.10b). Following the alignment, we removed PCR duplicates by leveraging the unique molecular identifiers with UMI tools.' Public accessions GSE54794 (RBFOX2 iCLIP in V6.5 mESCs) and SRP080878 (PTBP1/PTBP2 iCLIP) both resolve. All three tool versions are pinned. Params=1: the UMI barcode pattern/regex passed to umi_tools extract is not given, and the two datasets almost certainly use different UMI layouts, so the extraction cannot be reproduced as written.

iCLIP crosslink-site peak calling. Verbatim: 'Crosslinking sites were identified as peaks using Clipper, which was run within a Docker container based on the image brianyee/clipper:61d5456.' The image tag is a commit-like identifier, which is a real pin on the container content (though a tag, not an immutable digest); Clipper's own release version is not stated. Params=0: no Clipper invocation parameters are given at all - no --species/genome flag, no FDR or p-value threshold, no background/input specification, and no peak-merging settings, despite the peaks then being used quantitatively in C22 to validate motif predictions.

SplicePCA integration of the authors' data with the two developmental datasets, and the fitted developmental trajectory. Verbatim: 'we used the SplicePCA tool42 integrating our data set with the developmental data of Weyn-Vanhentenryck et al.4 and Liu et al.29. We selected events that did not have missing data for any sample and were significantly alternatively spliced in our data and the publicly available data. The developmental trajectory was fitted using spline regression with bootstrap resampling (n=500) to generate 95% confidence intervals. To investigate how splicing events are correlated with the principal components, we then computed the loading matrix A ... where V is the matrix of eigenvectors, L is a diagonal matrix with the corresponding eigenvalues.' Version=0: SplicePCA is cited only as reference 42 with no version, release, commit or URL anywhere in the paper - it is the one analysis tool here carrying no version information of any kind, and it produces the principal components that Figure 3 and the entire GSEA in C19 rest on. Params=1: the event-selection rule and the bootstrap count are given, but the spline-regression specification (degree, knots, smoothing) and the random seed are not.

Gene set enrichment analysis on the principal-component loadings. Verbatim: 'For each principal component, we then performed a gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) using the clusterProfiler package (version 4.8.1) in R v4.2.2 with the biological process ontology, miGSSize of 100, maxGSSize of 500, and an adjusted p-value cut-off of 0.05. The loadings for each gene on the respective principal component were used as input.' Package version, R version, ontology, both gene-set size bounds and the significance cut-off are stated. Params=1 because clusterProfiler's gseGO is permutation-based and neither the permutation count nor a random seed is given, and because the underlying GO annotation package and GO release date - which change the gene sets from month to month - are not named.

Direction-of-exon-inclusion assignment and chord-diagram visualisation. Verbatim: 'By intersecting our significant alternative splicing results with the Liu et al. data set, we assigned the Rbfox2-OE splicing events to three categories: 1) Neuronal direction when the exon inclusion level of the respective gene was significantly higher in neurons than in NPCs in the Liu et al. data; 2) NPC direction when the inclusion level was significantly lower in neurons than in NPC; 3) non-regulated, when the inclusion level was not significantly altered, or the splicing event was not detected. The results of this analysis were visualized with a chord diagram using the circlize package (version 0.4.15) in R.' The categorisation rule is clear and circlize is pinned; params=1 because the significance criteria applied to the Liu et al. comparison are not restated for this step and the event-matching rule (coordinate-exact vs gene-level) is not specified.

De novo pentamer motif enrichment in intronic flanks of regulated exons (custom analysis). Verbatim: 'The intronic sequences around alternatively spliced exons (enriched and suppressed exons separately) and a set of background sequences that were not alternatively spliced (FDR > 0.8 and |dPSI| < 0.1) were loaded from the mm39 reference genome (Gencode released 19.10.2022) using pysam (version 0.21). All possible pentameric sequences and their occurrence in the up- and downstream intronic sequences were counted in a sliding window of 50 nt. For each motif, we then subtracted its occurrence in the respective background sequences. Next, motif frequencies were transformed to z-scores using scipy. A motif was considered to be enriched when it had a z-score > 4 (p < 0.0001, two-sided z-test).' Background definition, window size, k-mer length and the z-score threshold are stated; params=1 because the length of the intronic flank actually scanned for THIS step is not given (C22 states 400 nt for the co-occurrence analysis and C23 states 150 nt exonic / 400 nt intronic for the localization map, but the enrichment step says only 'around'), and the custom code implementing it is not deposited.

Motif co-occurrence analysis with iCLIP and conservation filtering (custom analysis). Verbatim: '400 nt of intronic sequence flanking the alternatively spliced exon or the exon itself was loaded with pysam (version 0.21.0) and screened for the presence of a PTBP-associated CU-rich motifs (UCUCU, UUUCU, UCUUU, CUCUC, UCUCC, CUCUU, UUCCU)115 with a z-score > 4 upstream and RBFOX2 canonical motif downstream (GCAUG, UGCAU, CAUGC). Moreover, we integrated confirmed binding sites from the iClip data for RBFOX2, PTBP1, and PTBP2. We visualized this using an upset plot and only included overlapping sets with a minimum size of 1. Further, we examined evolutionarily conserved motif occurrences around these exons by filtering for motifs with a phastcons 35-way116 score > 0.8.' Flank length, the complete motif lists, the strand/position rule, the upset minimum set size and the conservation threshold are all explicit. The phastCons 35-way track is named but its UCSC assembly build and download date are not pinned, which is recorded as a gap-13 reference-resource issue rather than a params deduction.

Motif localization density map (custom analysis). Verbatim: 'we computed the motif density in a sliding window of 50 bp for all up- and downregulated events and background (non-regulated events). Motif density corresponds to the fraction of the 50 nt sliding window that is covered by the motif. The estimates were corrected by subtracting the background density for each motif. This analysis was limited to 150 nt of exonic and 400 nt of intronic sequences spanning up- and downstream from the intron/exon boundaries.' Window size, the density definition, the background-subtraction rule and both span limits are stated; the tool stack (pysam 0.21.0, numpy 1.23.5, Python 3.10.12) is inherited and pinned. Code is custom and not deposited.

Protein-interaction network retrieval. Verbatim: 'Potential interaction partners of RBFOX2 were identified with STRING using all potential interaction sources (version 12.0 beta) allowing 20 interacting proteins and showing confidence as edges. Interactions to RBFOX2 with a confidence score higher than 0.7 were considered high confidence.' The database version, the evidence-source setting, the interactor limit and the confidence cut-off are all stated. This is a hosted-service dependency executed through a web interface rather than a scripted API call, so it is reconstructable-by-hand (code=1) and the '12.0 beta' label is a moving pre-release target rather than a frozen release, which is why version stays at 1.

Overlap of alternatively spliced genes with neurodevelopmental-disorder risk genes. Verbatim: 'Alternatively spliced genes were intersected with high-confidence NDD genes from the GeneTrek database v3 to calculate the observed overlap. To obtain a null distribution of the expected overlap, 1317 genes (equal to the total number of alternatively spliced genes upon Rbfox2-OE) were randomly sampled from the universe of genes with annotated splice events and the overlap with high-confidence NDD genes and the p-value computed.' The database version, the sample size (1317), the sampling universe and the definition of the gene set are all stated; the seeded Monte Carlo machinery is scored separately at C26. GeneTrek v3 is named without an access date or a frozen download, recorded as a gap-13 issue.

Monte Carlo permutation testing of splicing-event and gene-set overlaps. Verbatim: 'In each simulation, a number of genes equal to the observed count of alternatively splicing events (tRbfox-KO and Ptbp2-KO) or genes (NDD risk genes) were randomly sampled from the universe of genes or splicing events. The overlap with the gene set of interest was then calculated. This process was repeated 100,000 times using a seed of 42 to generate a null distribution of expected overlaps. ... using Python (version 3.10.12), numpy (version 1.23.5), and scipy (version 1.10.1). CDF corresponds to the cumulative distribution function of the normal distribution.' This is the best-specified stochastic step in the paper: iteration count, an explicit random seed (42), the sampling universe, the p-value formula and three pinned library versions. Stage-1 cannot verify that the seed is actually CONSUMED by the code (rubric requires a shown-consumed seed), and there is no code to inspect, so the distributional-only clearance is asserted-but-unverified rather than granted.

Statistical analysis of immunohistochemistry measurements. Verbatim: 'Two groups were compared statistically using a t-test or a Wilcoxon test when assumptions of the parametric test were violated, and a data transformation did not improve the model fit. More than two groups were analyzed using one-way or two-way analysis of variance followed by Tukey's post hoc test or post hoc comparison of model means. Data were transformed using a loge or an arcsine square root transformation when assumptions of normality and homogeneity of variance were violated. ... Statistical analysis was performed using R v4.2.2 or Python (version 3.10.12) using scipy (version 1.10.1).' Params=1 because the test selection is described as a conditional decision procedure ('when assumptions are violated') without stating which assumption test, which threshold, or which branch was actually taken for each reported comparison, and because 'R v4.2.2 OR Python' leaves the implementation of each individual test undetermined. Data=1: the underlying per-cell/per-section counts may sit in Supplementary Data 1-6, but no source-data table is identified for these statistics.

ImageJ quantification of Western blot bands and confocal cell counts. Verbatim: 'Quantification of the bands was performed with ImageJ and normalized to GAPDH band intensity' and 'The images were analyzed, and the cells were counted using ImageJ software93.' Data=0: neither the raw Western blot images nor the confocal image stacks are deposited anywhere - no accession, no image repository, no supplementary raw-image archive is claimed. Version=0: no ImageJ or Fiji version, build or plugin set is named at either invocation. Params=0: no background-subtraction method, no ROI definition, no lane/band selection rule for the blots; no counting bin definition, no cortical-bin boundaries, no thresholding or segmentation settings, and no blinding/inclusion criteria for the cell counts. See granularity_note - this step is a borderline C/W classification and re-classifying it to W changes the denominator.

Mouse husbandry and in utero electroporation at E13.5 (Hes5::GFP and c57BL6/JRj mice, 4 ug/ul expression vectors, 5 pulses of 40 V, 50 ms, 950-ms intervals; license 23 177-07/G 13-1-089). Wet-lab, OOS.

Molecular cloning of the HA-Rbfox2 pCAGGS-mCherry construct, the miR-92a pcDNA3.1+ construct and the Rbfox2 3'UTR pGL3P reporter (all primer and oligonucleotide sequences given verbatim). Wet-lab, OOS.
N2A and HEK293 cell culture, calcium-phosphate and Transfectin transfections, and dual luciferase assays on a CentroXS LB 960 luminometer. Wet-lab, OOS.
RNA isolation (miRNeasy / High Pure), TaqMan miRNA and SYBR Green RT-qPCR normalised to U6 snRNA, and Western blotting with anti-RBFOX2 (Bethyl) and anti-GAPDH (ab8245). Wet-lab, OOS.
Cryosectioning, antigen retrieval, immunostaining with the enumerated primary/secondary antibody panel, and LSM710 confocal image acquisition with Zen software. Wet-lab, OOS.
Dissection of the GFP+ cortical area, trypsin dissociation, 100 um filtration and fluorescence-activated cell sorting of GFP+ cells for RNA-seq input. Wet-lab, OOS.
Illumina short-read library preparation (Clontech SMARTer Ultra Low Input, NuGEN Ovation Ultralow v2), Bioanalyzer/Qubit QC and NextSeq 500/550 sequencing of six pooled samples. Wet-lab, OOS.

Nanopore amplicon library preparation (EXP-PBC001 barcoding, SQK-LSK114 ligation kit, Herculase II target PCR with tailed primers, AMPure XP cleanups) and PromethION flow-cell sequencing. Wet-lab, OOS.

headline.static_readiness: 0/28 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 22/28 (78.6%) at Stage 1. This is the readiness upper bound (n_R-star + n_RI)/|S|, never 'reproducible'. The binding constraint on every one of the 22 RI steps is the version axis, capped at 1: this paper is an unusually diligent PROSE-PINNING paper with zero ENVIRONMENT CLOSURE. Twenty-five of twenty-eight computational steps carry an exact tool version in prose - BBDuk 39.01, STAR 2.7.10b, Subread 2.0.6, DESeq2 1.40.1, R 4.3.0, rMATS 4.1.2, numpy 1.23.5, pandas 2.0.1, Python 3.10.12, matplotlib 3.7.1, seaborn 0.12.2, upsetplot 0.9.0, Dorado 1.0.2, samtools 1.16.1, minimap2 2.26-r1175, pysam 0.21.0, lme4 1.1.37, car 3.1.3, scipy 1.10.1, scanpy 1.11.3, UMI-tools 1.1.4, clusterProfiler 4.8.1, R 4.2.2, circlize 0.4.15, STRING 12.0 beta, GeneTrek v3 - and the reference genome is pinned by dated release (Gencode mm39, released 19.10.2022). Under rubric Step 8's symmetric env-closure gate that is exact_pins_partial and therefore version=1, not 2: there is no lockfile, no conda or renv environment file, no requirements.txt, no image digest, no declared platform, and no channel/index specification anywhere in the paper. The paper also runs two different R interpreters (4.3.0 and 4.2.2) plus Python 3.10.12 with no per-step mapping of which package ran under which. The other axis holding every step at RI rather than R-star is code, which is 1 on all 28 steps for a single hard reason: THE PAPER CONTAINS NO CODE AVAILABILITY STATEMENT AND NO REPOSITORY OF ANY KIND. A full-text search of the JATS XML for github, gitlab, bitbucket, zenodo, softwareheritage, codeocean, osf.io and figshare returns exactly one hit, and it is a bibliographic citation for the pandas software DOI (10.5281/zenodo.8092754) in the reference list, not an artifact of this study. Substantial custom analysis code exists and is undeposited: the Nanopore exon-mapping read classifier, all three pentamer motif analyses, the direction-of-inclusion assignment, the loading-matrix computation and the Monte Carlo simulator. Because code is capped at 1 everywhere, a Stage-2 code read cannot lift a single step to R-star, which is exactly why stage2_candidate is false. Six steps fall to NI, and in five of the six the cause is params=0 rather than anything structural: rmats2sashimiplot invoked from an untagged Docker image with no parameters (C6), Dorado basecalling with no model named (C7), minimap2 with no preset named on data whose entire downstream analysis is exon-junction classification (C8), and Clipper with no invocation parameters at all (C17); the fifth, SplicePCA (C18), is the only analysis tool in the paper with no version information whatsoever, and it generates the principal components underlying Figure 3 and the GSEA. The sixth, ImageJ quantification (C28), is 0 on data, version and params simultaneously. Even if a Stage-2 code check recovered code=2 on every step, version would remain capped at 1 by the absence of env closure, so the R-star ceiling for this paper stays at 0/28 unless the authors ship a lock or an image digest.
headline.coverage: Computational coverage |S|/(|S|+|W|) = 28/36 = 77.8%. Eight wet-lab steps are OOS (mouse work and in utero electroporation, cloning, cell culture/luciferase, RT-qPCR/Western, immunostaining/confocal, FACS, Illumina library prep, Nanopore library prep). Note the borderline C28 classification described in granularity_note: re-classifying ImageJ quantification to W gives coverage 27/36 = 75.0% and an upper bound of 22/27 = 81.5%.

gaps.where: Whole paper. There is no Code availability section. The only availability statement in the article is 'Data availability: The RNA Sequencing data generated for this study are available on NCBI SRA (Sequence Read Archive) under the accession number PRJNA1013323.'
gaps.missing: No analysis code is deposited or linked anywhere. A full-text search of the bioRxiv JATS XML (2025/10/04 source.xml, v3) for github, gitlab, bitbucket, zenodo, softwareheritage, codeocean, osf.io and figshare yields a single hit - the pandas software citation 10.5281/zenodo.8092754 in the reference list - and no repository URL for this study. This is a finding recorded from the paper itself; no web search was performed to locate an unstated repository. Because of this, the code axis is 1 (reconstructable from prose) rather than 2 on all 28 computational steps, and it is the reason no step can reach R-star even after a Stage-2 read.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the analysis code (short-read pipeline driver, Nanopore classification scripts, motif analysis scripts, SplicePCA integration and plotting notebooks) in a public repository, archive a tagged release to Zenodo for a citable DOI, and add a Code availability statement to the manuscript.

gaps.where: Methods sections 'Nanopore RNA-sequencing analysis', 'Inferring the direction of exon inclusion', 'Motif enrichment analysis', 'Motif co-occurrence analysis', 'Motif localization map', 'Inferring the alternative splicing trajectory during cortical development', 'Monte Carlo Simulation' (steps C9, C18, C20, C21, C22, C23, C26)
gaps.missing: Seven steps are bespoke analyses implemented by the authors rather than off-the-shelf tool invocations, and none of the implementations is public. Specifically undeposited: the exon-mapping read classifier that assigns Nanopore reads to inclusion/skipping (the sole evidence for the miR-92a splicing result); the exhaustive pentamer counting and z-scoring code with its 50 nt sliding window; the co-occurrence screen against the enumerated CU-rich and GCAUG motif lists with phastCons filtering; the motif density localization map; the loading-matrix computation A = V L^(1/2) applied to the SplicePCA output; the direction-of-inclusion three-way assignment; and the 100,000-iteration Monte Carlo sampler. The prose descriptions are unusually detailed for custom code, which is why these steps still score code=1 (reconstructable) rather than 0, but reconstruction is not reproduction.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the custom scripts with the input intermediate files they consume (in particular the rMATS output tables and the target-exon coordinate lists), so the classification and motif analyses can be re-run rather than re-implemented.

gaps.where: Entire computational environment; all 28 computational steps
gaps.missing: No environment capture of any kind exists. Absent: conda-lock / pixi.lock / renv.lock / requirements.txt / environment.yml / Dockerfile for the authors' own stack; no declared platform (linux-64 or otherwise); no package channel or index specification; and no digest for either of the two containers used. The paper also mixes three interpreters - R 4.3.0 (DESeq2), R 4.2.2 (clusterProfiler, IHC statistics) and Python 3.10.12 - without stating which interpreter ran lme4 1.1.37, car 3.1.3 or circlize 0.4.15. Under rubric Step 8 this is exactly the 'scattered == pins in prose without interpreter+channel+platform' case, so version is capped at 1 with subtier exact_pins_partial on every step that has pins at all. This single gap is what holds static_readiness at 0/28 despite the paper's otherwise strong version discipline.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock or renv.lock covering the declared platform, or a container built from the actual analysis environment referenced by immutable digest, and state which interpreter each package set ran under.

gaps.where: Gap subtype 2a (version absent). Methods sections 'Inferring the alternative splicing trajectory during cortical development' (SplicePCA, step C18), 'Analysis of publicly available iClip data sets' (Clipper, step C17), 'RNA-sequencing analysis' (rmats2sashimiplot, step C6), 'RT-qPCR and Western blot' and 'Immunostaining and Imaging' (ImageJ, step C28), and 'Nanopore RNA-sequencing analysis' (unstated R interpreter for lme4/car, step C10)
gaps.missing: Five named tools carry no version string. SplicePCA is cited only as reference 42 with no version, release, commit or URL - and it produces the principal components on which Figure 3 and the entire C19 gene-set enrichment depend, which is why C18 is the only step scoring version=0 among the analysis tools. Clipper's release version is absent (only the container tag is given). rmats2sashimiplot's version is absent. ImageJ/Fiji version and plugin set are absent at both invocations. The R interpreter version for the lme4/car mixed-effects analysis is absent while two other R versions appear elsewhere in the same Methods. Additionally, Dorado 1.0.2 is pinned but its basecalling MODEL - which determines read accuracy and therefore the exon-mapping classification - is not named, a version-shaped omission recorded here as well as in the C7 params score.
gaps.how_to_close: State a version or commit for SplicePCA, Clipper, rmats2sashimiplot and ImageJ; name the Dorado basecalling model and its version; and state the R interpreter used for every R package invocation.

gaps.where: Gap subtype 2b (floating version lower bound / mutable reference). Methods 'RNA-sequencing analysis': 'Sashimi plots were created using rmats2sashimiplot within a Docker container using the image xinglab/rmats2sashimiplot' (step C6); and Methods 'STRING network analysis': 'STRING ... (version 12.0 beta)' (step C24)
gaps.missing: The rmats2sashimiplot image reference carries neither a tag nor a digest, so it resolves to a mutable :latest that can change content between pulls - this is the only genuinely floating software reference in an otherwise well-pinned paper, and it is recorded with subflag workflow-ref-unpinned. By contrast the iCLIP container brianyee/clipper:61d5456 does carry a commit-like tag, which is a real (if not immutable) pin. STRING '12.0 beta' names a pre-release that is by definition a moving target and is queried through a hosted web interface with no API call or query date recorded.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin the rmats2sashimiplot image by sha256 digest, prefer digests over tags for the Clipper image as well, and record the STRING release (non-beta) plus the query date.

gaps.where: Reference resources consumed across steps C19 (GO annotation for clusterProfiler), C22 (phastCons 35-way conservation track), C24 (STRING 12.0 beta), C25 (GeneTrek v3). Contrast with C2/C16/C21, where the reference genome IS pinned: 'the Gencode reference genome of Mus musculus mm39 (released 19.10.2022)'.
gaps.missing: Four external reference resources are consumed out-of-band without a version-and-date pin. The GO biological-process gene sets behind the GSEA are named by ontology only, with no org.Mm.eg.db version and no GO release date, although GO gene-set membership changes on a monthly cadence and directly determines which terms are enriched. The phastCons 35-way track is named without a UCSC assembly build or download date. STRING is queried as a live hosted service. GeneTrek is given as 'v3' with no access date or frozen snapshot. Per collection protocol Delta-B these would carry env_capture_class B or C, but that classification requires reading the executable workflow, which does not exist here and is Stage-2 in any case, so every step is recorded as env_capture_class n/a.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin every reference resource by release identifier plus retrieval date, and deposit frozen copies (or their checksums) of the GO, phastCons and GeneTrek snapshots actually used.

gaps.where: Steps C15 (scipy bootstrap, n=1,000), C18 (SplicePCA spline regression bootstrap, n=500), C19 (clusterProfiler gseGO permutation test). Contrast with step C26, Methods 'Monte Carlo Simulation': 'This process was repeated 100,000 times using a seed of 42'.
gaps.missing: Three stochastic procedures run without a stated random seed, so their outputs (the 95% confidence bands on the pseudotime expression splines, the 95% bands on the developmental trajectory, and the GSEA enrichment p-values) are reproducible only distributionally, not exactly. These steps carry the distributional-only subflag and are capped at RI by the rubric's stochastic ceiling independently of the version cap. The single Monte Carlo step that DOES declare a seed (42) is the counterexample and shows the authors were aware of the issue; however, Stage-1 cannot verify that the seed is actually consumed by the code, and the rubric grants the clearance only when consumption is shown, which requires code that does not exist here.
gaps.how_to_close: Set and report an explicit seed for the two bootstrap procedures and for the GSEA permutation test, and show in the deposited code where each seed is consumed.

gaps.where: Data availability: 'The RNA Sequencing data generated for this study are available on NCBI SRA (Sequence Read Archive) under the accession number PRJNA1013323.' Methods 'RNA-sequencing': 'All six samples were pooled in equimolar ratio and sequenced on an Illumina NextSeq 500/550 device.' Methods 'Nanopore Amplicon Library Preparation and Sequencing' and 'Nanopore RNA-sequencing analysis' (steps C7-C10).
gaps.missing: Two distinct sample-correspondence problems. (1) The accession does not resolve to enumerable runs - see the liveness block - so the mapping from the six sequenced samples to the Rbfox2-OE and control conditions cannot be recovered from the archive, and it is not given in the paper either. This is why data=1 rather than 2 on every step consuming the authors' own sequencing. (2) The Nanopore amplicon data are not covered by any stated accession: the Data availability sentence names 'The RNA Sequencing data', while the ENA record for PRJNA1013323 describes the project as bulk RNA-seq of in-utero-electroporated cortical cells only, with no mention of Nanopore or PromethION. The raw pod5 files that steps C7-C10 consume therefore have no identified deposition, and neither do the per-sample barcode-to-condition assignments for the miR-92a overexpression comparison.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the runs under PRJNA1013323 with a sample-to-condition table, deposit the Nanopore pod5/FASTQ data under a stated accession with the barcode-to-sample mapping, and cite both accessions explicitly in Data availability.

gaps.where: Data availability: 'The RNA Sequencing data generated for this study are available on NCBI SRA (Sequence Read Archive) under the accession number PRJNA1013323.' Checked 2026-07-28.
gaps.missing: The paper's sole primary-data accession does not currently yield retrievable reads at either archive. NCBI Entrez returns zero hits for PRJNA1013323 in db=bioproject (both as a plain term and as 1013323[BioProject Accession]) and zero hits in db=sra for the project or its title, while control queries in the same session resolve normally (PRJNA398545 -> 1 hit; GSE96950 -> 6 hits), so this is not an eutils outage. ENA holds a mirrored project stub that resolves 200 and is marked ENA-STATUS PUBLIC (center 'Johannes Gutenberg-University Mainz', title 'Early Rbfox2 overexpression hijacks the Ptbp splicing program to drive premature neuronal migration during early cortical development'), but its XML contains no linked SAMPLE or RUN elements. BOUNDED CLAIM: the ENA portal filereport endpoint returned HTTP 500 throughout the check window (an EBI-side outage affecting all queries, not just this accession), so run enumeration via ENA could not be completed and the possibility that runs exist but are not currently enumerable cannot be fully excluded. No redundancy-rescue mirror was found. Recorded as link/accession rot rather than as fabrication.
gaps.how_to_close: Confirm the release status of PRJNA1013323 with SRA, ensure the runs are indexed and public, and re-verify resolution from both NCBI and ENA before final publication.

gaps.where: Methods sections 'Animals', 'Constructs', 'Cell Culture, transfections, and luciferase assays', 'RT-qPCR and Western blot', 'In utero Electroporation', 'Immunostaining and Imaging', 'RNA-sequencing' (library prep), 'Nanopore Amplicon Library Preparation and Sequencing' (steps W1-W8)
gaps.missing: Eight non-computational wet-lab steps are out of scope for a NASEM-2019 computational-reproducibility assessment and are excluded from |S|. They are recorded because they set the computational coverage denominator at 28/36 = 77.8%. For completeness: the wet-lab protocols are described to a high standard (full primer and oligonucleotide sequences, catalogue numbers for every antibody, electroporation pulse settings, kit part numbers EXP-PBC001 and SQK-LSK114, and the animal license number), so the OOS classification reflects scope, not documentation quality.
gaps.how_to_close: n/a - out of scope by routing. No action required for the computational assessment.

gaps.where: Methods 'RNA-sequencing analysis': 'Sashimi plots were created using rmats2sashimiplot within a Docker container using the image xinglab/rmats2sashimiplot. Due to its MISO backend, PSI values may differ from rMATS results.' (step C6)
gaps.missing: The authors themselves disclose a known numerical inconsistency between the figure-generating tool and the analysis that the figure illustrates: rmats2sashimiplot computes PSI through a MISO backend that can disagree with the rMATS 4.1.2 values reported in the text. This is honest disclosure rather than a concealed defect, and it is recorded here as a known-behaviour issue in published tooling rather than as an author error. The reproducibility consequence is concrete: a re-runner comparing sashimi-plot PSI values against the reported rMATS PSI values will observe mismatches that are expected, and nothing in the paper states which of the two numbers each figure panel displays.
gaps.how_to_close: State which PSI values each sashimi panel displays, and report the rMATS PSI alongside the plot so the two are not confused.

liveness.network_context: Unauthenticated curl with a browser user agent, plus NCBI eutils JSON and the ENA browser XML API.
